derivation:
  setup: >-
    Fix E/Q. Write r = rank(E(Q)), and work with F2 = Z/2Z-dimensions
    throughout. The unconditional 2-descent theorem (Galois cohomology of
    the multiplication-by-2 sequence 0 -> E[2] -> E -> E -> 0 over Q, taking
    Q-points and the long exact sequence in group cohomology) gives a short
    exact sequence of F2-vector spaces / abelian groups:

      0 -> E(Q)/2E(Q) -> Sel_2(E) -> Sha(E)[2] -> 0        (*)

    This sequence is a theorem, not a conjecture: it requires no BSD, no
    GRH, and no assumption that Sha(E) is finite. Sel_2(E) is itself
    unconditionally finite (a standard fact from the descent construction:
    it is bounded by a finite computation over a finite set of places), so
    (*) forces Sha(E)[2] to be finite too, as a quotient of a finite group
    -- this is a *consequence* of (*), not an input to it, and in
    particular it needs nothing beyond (*) itself. Full finiteness of
    Sha(E) (all primes, not just 2) is a strictly stronger, still-open
    statement and is never invoked below.

    E(Q)_tors trivial means E(Q) is torsion-free, so as an abstract group
    E(Q) ~= Z^r, and therefore E(Q)/2E(Q) ~= (Z/2Z)^r exactly:
      dim_F2 E(Q)/2E(Q) = r.
    (If torsion were nontrivial with even order this identity would need a
    correction term; it is not needed here since torsion is given trivial.)

    31 certified Z-independent rational points witness a rank-31 subgroup
    of E(Q), so unconditionally, directly from their existence (no descent
    needed for this half):
      r >= 31.

    Let d = dim_F2 Sel_2(E) (the given, exactly-computed quantity), and
    let s = dim_F2 Sha(E)[2] >= 0. From (*), dimension-counting an exact
    sequence of finite F2-vector spaces gives:
      d = r + s,  i.e.  r = d - s.                          (**)

  part_i_dim_equals_31: >-
    Set d = 31 in (**): r = 31 - s. Since s >= 0, this gives r <= 31. Given
    independently r >= 31 (the 31 certified points), the two bounds force

      s = 0  and  r = 31  EXACTLY.

    This is the strict implication: dim Sel_2(E) = 31 (with the 31
    certified points and trivial torsion already in hand) forces
    rank(E(Q)) = 31 exactly -- no 32nd independent point can exist, because
    any such point would raise r past the ceiling r <= 31 that d = 31
    imposes via (**). As a corollary, not an assumption, Sha(E)[2] = 0 is
    proved, not merely conjectured.

    Conjecture dependency: NONE. Every step is (*)  plus  elementary
    F2-linear-algebra dimension counting on a short exact sequence, plus the
    torsion-triviality identity dim E(Q)/2E(Q) = r, plus the given r >= 31
    from certified points. No use of BSD (no L-function, no analytic rank,
    anywhere in this argument), no use of GRH, no assumption that Sha(E) is
    finite (only Sha(E)[2] appears, and its finiteness is a corollary of
    (*), not a hypothesis).

    The one non-conjectural but load-bearing PRECONDITION (not a
    mathematical conjecture, a correctness precondition on the computation
    itself): the group actually computed "over S" must equal the true
    Sel_2(E) that (*) is a statement about. Concretely, S must be large
    enough that the descent map factors through H^1(G_{Q,S}, E[2]) and every
    local condition needed to cut H^1(G_{Q,S}, E[2]) down to Sel_2(E) is
    actually imposed at every place in S -- standardly this requires S to
    contain 2, the archimedean place, and every prime of bad reduction for
    E. If S omits a place where a nontrivial local condition would apply,
    the group computed is not provably equal to Sel_2(E), and (**) cannot be
    invoked for it. I have deliberately not adjudicated whether the S used
    by any protocol satisfies this, since doing so would require reading
    material I am blind to; I flag it here as the dependency the closure
    reading rests on beyond pure math, exactly because J1's attack plan (an
    owned joint I am not assigned, per review-plan.yaml) names checking this
    as its own task.

  part_ii_dim_geq_32: >-
    Set d >= 32 in (**): r = d - s with s >= 0, so s ranges over
    [0, d - 31] given the independent floor r >= 31 (i.e. s <= d - 31 is
    required to keep r >= 31). Correspondingly r ranges over the full
    interval [31, d]:

      - if s = d - 31 (Sha(E)[2] absorbs the entire excess Selmer
        dimension beyond 31), then r = 31: no 32nd independent point
        exists, despite d >= 32.
      - if s = 0, then r = d: a full complement of new independent points
        exists.
      - any intermediate s gives an intermediate r.

    So dim Sel_2(E) >= 32 is CONSISTENT with r = 31 and is CONSISTENT with
    r = d, and with every integer value in between. It does not, by itself,
    determine r. What it strictly LICENSES is only the logical possibility
    that up to (d - 31) further Z-independent rational points exist beyond
    the certified 31 -- i.e. it licenses a bounded search for such points
    (bounded by d - 31 additional independent generators, since r <= d is
    forced by (**) with s >= 0). What it does NOT license is any assertion
    about which case obtains: neither "a 32nd point exists" nor "r = 31
    despite d >= 32" follows from d >= 32 alone.

    Two ways to resolve the ambiguity, both by direct mathematical content
    of (*)/(**), stated for completeness though outside the strict
    re-derivation asked for:
      (a) Exhibit and certify an actual further Z-independent rational
          point (or points). This raises the certified floor on r directly
          and unconditionally -- it is not descent, it is a direct rank
          witness exactly as the original 31 points were -- and if the new
          certified count reaches d, the closure argument of part (i)
          re-applies verbatim with r >= d in place of r >= 31, forcing
          s = 0 and r = d exactly.
      (b) Independently bound or compute dim Sha(E)[2] (e.g. via a further
          descent, such as visualising Sha via an auxiliary isogenous
          curve, or a higher n-descent). This is generically hard and is
          not the same computation as the 2-descent already performed; it
          is not supplied "for free" by BSD or GRH either (see dependency
          discussion below).
    Absent (a) or (b), the honest state given only d >= 32 is: r is
    undetermined in [31, d]. This is not evidence of failure -- it is the
    correct content of (**) when s is not otherwise pinned down.

    Conjecture dependency: NONE for the "licenses, does not guarantee"
    reading itself -- it is again pure dimension-counting on (*). No
    conjecture licenses jumping from d >= 32 to a definite value of r
    without further computation as in (a) or (b); in particular BSD does
    not supply Sha(E)[2] or its order without its own separate (and, for
    the full BSD formula, itself-conjectural) machinery, and does not
    substitute for either (a) or (b).

  part_iii_dependency_set: >-
    Complete list of conjectures load-bearing anywhere in this derivation:
    NONE. Explicitly, for the record:
      - BSD (Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, in any form -- rank conjecture or
        full refined formula): NOT invoked. No L-function, analytic rank,
        or L-value enters this argument at any point; rank is bounded
        purely by algebraic 2-descent (*) and the direct point-independence
        certification, never by an analytic proxy.
      - GRH (Generalized Riemann Hypothesis): NOT invoked. GRH could only
        become relevant to an auxiliary EFFECTIVITY question (e.g. an
        effective bound on when a search for bad primes or a class-group
        computation used to build S is complete), never to the logical
        content of (*) or (**) themselves, which are unconditional
        Galois-cohomology statements. No such effectivity question is part
        of the quantity asked to be re-derived.
      - Finiteness of Sha(E) (the general Tate-Shafarevich finiteness
        conjecture): NOT invoked. Only Sha(E)[2] appears, and its
        finiteness is an unconditional COROLLARY of (*) (a subquotient of
        the finite group Sel_2(E)), not a hypothesis borrowed from the
        general conjecture. The general conjecture is strictly stronger and
        remains open regardless of this derivation.
    The only load-bearing items outside pure mathematics are (1) the given
    facts themselves -- E(Q)_tors trivial, the 31 certified independent
    points, and "dim Sel_2(E) computed exactly over S equals [31 | >=32]"
    -- taken as hypotheses exactly as stated in the task, and (2) for
    reading (i) only, the computational-correctness precondition on S
    stated above (S must be sufficient for the computed group to equal true
    Sel_2(E)), which is an implementation-correctness question I am blind
    to and do not adjudicate here, flagged instead as the dependency the
    closure argument rests on beyond the exact sequence itself.
